leads.headline: Attacks on Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
leads.body: Fresh attacks on commercial ships raised global energy supply fears. Iran vowed to use all available means against a US blockade; a Houthi strike on Riyadh and interceptions over Saudi Arabia also threatened the Red Sea.

leads.headline: Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in a Libyan Port
leads.body: Ukrainian drones sank the warship in Benghazi and hit cargo ships from the Mediterranean to the Baltic: Kyiv's longest-range war campaign. Two Libyan naval officers were killed, raising fears of wider Mediterranean escalation.

leads.headline: Zelensky: Ukraine Needs €115 Billion for 2027
leads.body: Kyiv seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for the state and war through 2027. The US defence secretary paused Patriot missile supplies; Washington shelved business-deal plans with Russia to end the war.

leads.headline: Pakistan's First Astronaut Reaches China's Space Station
leads.body: China's crewed launch took Pakistan's first astronaut to its orbiting space station, a milestone watched live across Pakistan. The flight deepens their space partnership and marks Islamabad's first human presence in orbit.

leads.headline: Australia Signs Landmark Treaty with Solomon Islands
leads.body: Australia and Solomon Islands signed a major treaty strengthening Canberra's Pacific security position and reshaping regional alignments, as Pacific capitals weigh competing partnerships and promises.

leads.headline: US Jury Convicts Huawei of Stealing Trade Secrets
leads.body: A New York jury convicted Chinese firm Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets but acquitted it of racketeering. Beijing accused Washington of obstructing Chinese firms in the tech cold war's latest legal clash.

leads.headline: Anthropic Shares Fall Below Their IPO Price
leads.body: Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price for the first time, wiping out its $1 trillion valuation as AI fears returned to Wall Street. Asian markets fell first; US futures followed lower.

leads.headline: Colombia Frees All Hostages in Supermarket Siege
leads.body: Colombian security forces stormed a Cartagena supermarket, freeing every hostage and ending a siege that gripped the country. President Petro said one assailant was killed and all captives survived.

leads.headline: Court Gives Senegal Its Africa Cup Title Back
leads.body: Sport's highest court restored Senegal's 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title on appeal. Morocco, stripped of the crown, vowed to challenge the ruling.

leads.headline: UK Energy Bills to Jump 26% in January
leads.body: Regulator Ofgem's energy price cap rise, driven by surging gas prices, lifts a typical annual bill from £1,723 to £2,166 in January, Britain's coldest, darkest winter month.

briefs.headline: EURO INFLATION
briefs.body: Eurostat: euro-area inflation rose to 4.0%; growth, jobs and output data were mixed.

briefs.headline: AUSTRALIA PRICES
briefs.body: Fuel costs lifted Australian inflation to 4.9%; the central bank is still expected to hold interest rates.

briefs.headline: EU TECH FUND
briefs.body: The EU plans a €50 billion tech fund to challenge US and Chinese dominance.

briefs.headline: GTA VI
briefs.body: GTA VI's $3.79 billion debut had Zuckerberg joking and Musk laughing; Take-Two investors still want more.

briefs.headline: EASYJET
briefs.body: EasyJet profit fell 89% after a £244 million fuel-cost hit; it is retiring its oldest aircraft faster.

briefs.headline: AMAZON BUYS DECART
briefs.body: Amazon bought AI startup Decart, betting better software can help its chips compete with Nvidia's.

briefs.headline: AI-AGENT HACK
briefs.body: Amazon says attackers used AI agents with little human input to breach a university server through a previously unknown flaw.

briefs.headline: CIA BREACH
briefs.body: Hackers breached unclassified CIA and ODNI intelligence-analysis systems, the New York Times reported.

briefs.headline: GAZA
briefs.body: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed seven people, including a senior security official.

briefs.headline: RIYADH
briefs.body: A Houthi attack injured 11 in Riyadh, including two Indians. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted more attacks after striking Hodeidah.

briefs.headline: KOREA
briefs.body: South Korea said Russian jets entered its air defence identification zone.

briefs.headline: NORTH KOREA
briefs.body: North Korea declared a Swiss diplomat persona non grata and ordered him out.

briefs.headline: XI PURGE
briefs.body: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption purge ousted Chen Jining, Shanghai's party chief and a rising political star.

briefs.headline: BANGLADESH
briefs.body: Bangladesh garment workers won a 36% pay rise after weeks of protests.

briefs.headline: INDONESIA MINE
briefs.body: Rescuers sought dozens of miners trapped in a flooded Indonesian gold mine.

briefs.headline: HIV WARNING
briefs.body: The UN warned funding cuts threaten decades of progress against HIV and AIDS.

briefs.headline: ÁBREGO GARCÍA
briefs.body: Kilmar Ábrego García left the US for Spain, ending a 20-month legal fight that made him a Trump-era deportation symbol.

briefs.headline: GIVING
briefs.body: After $26 billion in gifts, MacKenzie Scott gave Atlanta students another $8 million; she is still worth $27 billion.
